Prompt Pixaroma (3. what goes in the new parts)

promptState.text: Remove the two plain grey bars at the left and the right sides: paint over them completely so that no grey is left, and the whole frame is one continuous wide photograph. In the left part: more of the blue sky with small white clouds, the rocky coastline and the calm blue sea, and the white terrace wall and stone floor running on. In the right part: the white house wall and the red tile roof running on, and the stone floor. The picture between the two bars does not move: the house, the blue door, the armchair and the table stay exactly where they are, at the same size.

 P-H3 Image needs ComfyUI 0.44.0 or newer, the first version with these nodes. On an older ComfyUI the nodes show red: update ComfyUI first.

 Load Diffusion Model

 LoRA (in LoRA Loader Pixaroma)

Download p-h3-image_lora_bf16.safetensors1.82 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/loras/h3

Create the h3 folder inside loras if it does not exist.

 Load CLIP

Download p-h3-image_text_encoder_int8_convrot.safetensors4.77 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/text_encoders

 Load VAE

Download p-h3-image_vae_int8_convrot.safetensors2.93 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/vae

P-H3 Image is built on MiniMax H3, so the MiniMax H3 Community License applies. Read it and check what it says for your country before you use the model.

{"version":1,"content":"

HOW TO USE

Make a picture wider or taller: the model paints more of the scene around it, and your picture stays exactly as it is in the middle. The demo turns a square photo of a Greek house into a wide 16:9 picture with more of the coast.

 Steps

  1. Load your picture in Load Image Mini Pixaroma.
  2. On Outpaint Pixaroma, pick the new shape, or add space to the sides you want.
  3. Change what goes in the new parts in Prompt Pixaroma.
  4. Leave the seed on F to repeat a result, or switch it to R to try a new one every Run.
  5. Press Run. Drag across Image Compare Pixaroma to see before and after.

 Writing the prompt

  1. Name the grey parts as something to paint over: Remove the two plain grey bars at the left and the right sides: paint over them completely so that no grey is left. If you add space at the top or bottom, say so.
  2. Say what goes in each part: In the left part: more of the blue sky with small white clouds, the rocky coastline and the calm blue sea ... In the right part: the white house wall and the red tile roof running on.
  3. End by holding the middle in place, and name what is in it: The picture between the two bars does not move: the house, the blue door, the armchair and the table stay exactly where they are, at the same size.

 Good to know

  • The wording decides. With keep the picture in the middle unchanged the bars stayed grey on 4 of 4 seeds: the model kept them as part of the picture. Calling them bars to paint over filled them on 4 of 4.
  • The middle can slide. Without the last sentence the picture moved sideways on 3 of 4 seeds. With it, it held still on 9 of 12 runs. On a seed that slides, the stitched result shows the door twice with a blurred join: try another seed.
  • Your picture stays your picture. We compared the result with the input: past the 64 px soft edge the middle is the same, pixel for pixel.
  • The limit changes the work size, not the result. On Outpaint Pixaroma, limits 1, 2 and 4 all came out at 2844 x 1600 for our 1600 x 1600 picture, because Outpaint Stitch brings the result up to full size. The new parts are sharpest at 4.
  • The new parts are different on every seed: other hills, other clouds, a house or none.

 Something not working?

Each button opens the answer on the Pixaroma help page.

Save to your own folder Nodes look different from the video

{"version":1,"content":"

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the Download Models note.

  • Load Diffusion Model (MiniMax H3 fl2va) - MiniMax H3, the video model. The LoRA in the next node turns it into P-H3 Image, a picture model. If you did Episode 41 you may already have this file.
  • LoRA Loader Pixaroma (P-H3 Image) - The P-H3 Image LoRA from Pruna. Keep it on at strength 1: without it H3 is a video model and the picture falls apart.
  • Load CLIP (P-H3 Image text encoder) - Reads your prompt and turns the words into something the model understands. The type must be minimax.
  • Load VAE (P-H3 Image VAE) - Turns the finished render into the picture. It is made for P-H3 Image, a different file from the H3 video VAE.

 The steps you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you need to touch.

  • Load Image Mini Pixaroma (1. your picture) - The picture to extend. Click it to upload your own, or pick one from the list.
  • Outpaint Pixaroma (2. the new shape) - Adds flat grey #808080 bars around your picture up to the new shape, here 16:9 from a square picture, and makes the whole canvas about 4 megapixels. Pick another shape or add space to any side on the node. Lower the limit to 1 or 2 for a faster Run.
  • Prompt Pixaroma (3. what goes in the new parts) - Keep the first sentence, then change what goes in the left and right parts and what the last sentence names (see How to Use).
  • Seed Pixaroma (4. fixed or random) - The seed. F (fixed) repeats the result, R (random) tries a new one every Run. The demo uses seed 3.

 The helpers

Purple. They run by themselves and do the small jobs between the steps.

  • Outpaint Stitch Pixaroma (puts your picture back) - Makes the result as big as the padded canvas at full size and puts your ORIGINAL picture back in the middle, so that part stays exactly your picture. Only the new parts are painted by the model. A 64 px soft edge and a colour match hide the join.

 Working in the background

Teal. They run by themselves. The line next to each one says if there is anything worth changing.

  • MiniMaxH3SigmaShift (1 / 1 for pictures) - The noise schedule. P-H3 Image needs 1 and 1. Leave it as it is.

 The work

Green. They run by themselves.

  • PH3 Image Conditioning (prompt + the padded canvas) - Joins the prompt and the padded canvas. With width and height on 0, the result has the size and shape of the padded canvas.
  • Basic Guider (no CFG) - Hands the model and the prompt to the sampler. P-H3 Image needs no CFG and no negative prompt.
  • KSampler Select (sampler) - The sampler. euler is the one in Pruna's own workflow. ComfyUI's template uses er_sde: the same speed, but it broke small words on a label in our tests.
  • Manual Sigmas (the 8 steps) - The 8 steps the model was trained on. More steps do not help, so leave these numbers as they are.
  • Random Noise - The starting noise, from the seed.
  • Sampler Custom Advanced (the render) - The render itself: 8 steps. The normal KSampler cannot take this hand-made step list, so this node does the job.
  • VAE Decode (latent to picture) - Turns the finished render into a picture.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Save Image Pixaroma (saves the result) - Saves each result as PNG into ComfyUI/output/P-H3 Image Outpaint and shows it on the node.
  • Image Compare Pixaroma (before and after, drag across it) - The canvas with its grey bars and the result on top of each other. Drag across it to see the new parts appear, and to check that the middle stayed in place.

 Readouts

Dark. Nothing to set: they show you what happened.

  • Run Timer - The dark clock above the result shows how long the last Run took.

widgets_values:
{"version":1,"content":"

RUN TIMES

Measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow, with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: a smaller picture is much faster.

Limit on Outpaint PixaromaTime
1 megapixelabout 8 s
2 megapixelsabout 10 s
4 megapixels (the demo)about 19 s

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI also has to load the models (about 20 GB for H3, and 10 GB for the LoRA, the text encoder and the VAE), so it takes longer. After that they stay in memory, if your PC has enough of it. Two testers with 16 GB cards: with 64 GB of RAM the next Runs were close to the times above; with 32 GB the models loaded from disk again on every Run, and each Run took about 4 times as long.

 On a smaller card

Set the limit on Outpaint Pixaroma to 1.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Run Times","icon":"run-timer","color":"#3f9a4f"}}
